title: ISP Tracking & DNS Privacy for Beginners
metaDescription: Learn how ISPs track your internet activity and sell your data. Complete guide to DNS privacy, encrypted DNS setup, and protecting yourself from ISP monitoring.
intro: Your internet service provider (ISP) can see every website you visit, even in incognito mode. They often sell this data to advertisers and may throttle your connection based on your activity. This guide shows you how to protect your privacy with encrypted DNS and other privacy tools.
prerequisites: Access to your device's network settings
Administrative rights on your computer or mobile device

steps.title: Understand What Your ISP Can See
steps.description: Before protecting yourself, it's important to understand exactly what information your ISP can access about your internet usage.
actions: Review your ISP's privacy policy to see what data they collect
Check if your ISP sells browsing data to third parties
Use a DNS leak test website to see your current DNS provider
Document your current internet speeds for later comparison
steps.proTip: Most major ISPs like Comcast, Verizon, and AT&T have explicit policies allowing them to sell your browsing data unless you opt out.

steps.title: Choose an Encrypted DNS Provider
steps.description: Replace your ISP's DNS servers with privacy-focused alternatives that encrypt your DNS queries and don't log your activity.
actions: Research reputable DNS providers like Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), Quad9, or NextDNS
Compare their privacy policies and logging practices
Note down the DNS server addresses you want to use
Consider DNS providers that offer malware and ad blocking features
steps.proTip: Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 is fastest for most users, while Quad9 offers better malware protection.

steps.title: Configure DNS Settings on Your Router
steps.description: Setting up encrypted DNS at the router level protects all devices on your network automatically.
actions: Access your router's admin panel (usually at 192.168.1.1 or 192.168.0.1)
Navigate to DNS or Network settings
Replace ISP DNS servers with your chosen encrypted DNS addresses
Save settings and restart your router to apply changes
steps.proTip: Router-level DNS changes protect smart TVs, IoT devices, and guest devices that you can't configure individually.
steps.warning: Some ISPs block or redirect DNS changes. If this doesn't work, you may need to configure individual devices instead.

steps.title: Enable DNS over HTTPS in Your Browser
steps.description: Modern browsers support DNS over HTTPS (DoH), which encrypts DNS queries even if your ISP tries to intercept them.
actions: Open your browser settings (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge)
Find the Privacy/Security section
Enable 'DNS over HTTPS' or 'Secure DNS' option
Select your preferred DNS provider from the list or enter custom addresses
steps.proTip: Use Incognito Browser for additional privacy protection alongside encrypted DNS - it blocks tracking scripts that regular DNS changes can't prevent.

steps.title: Configure Mobile Device DNS Settings
steps.description: Protect your smartphone and tablet from ISP tracking by configuring encrypted DNS on mobile devices.
actions: Install a DNS configuration app like 1.1.1.1 or NextDNS
Alternatively, manually configure DNS in WiFi settings
Test that the new DNS settings work on both WiFi and mobile data
Enable the 'Private DNS' option on Android devices
steps.proTip: Mobile carriers also track your DNS queries. Using encrypted DNS protects you on both WiFi and cellular connections.

steps.title: Test Your DNS Privacy Setup
steps.description: Verify that your DNS changes are working properly and that you're protected from common DNS leaks.
actions: Visit dnsleaktest.com to check if your new DNS servers are being used
Run both standard and extended DNS leak tests
Use ipleak.net to verify no DNS queries are going to your ISP
Test browsing speed to ensure the new DNS doesn't slow you down
steps.proTip: If tests show your ISP's DNS servers, clear your DNS cache and restart your devices before testing again.

steps.title: Consider Additional Privacy Protection
steps.description: While encrypted DNS helps with privacy, your ISP can still see which websites you visit through other methods. Layer additional protection for comprehensive privacy.
actions: Research VPN services that have strict no-logging policies
Consider using the Tor browser for sensitive browsing
Use privacy-focused browsers like Incognito Browser for daily browsing
Enable HTTPS-only mode in your browsers to encrypt web traffic
steps.warning: Free VPNs often log and sell your data just like ISPs do. Only use reputable paid VPN services with proven no-logging policies.

pro_tips: Combine encrypted DNS with a reputable VPN service for maximum privacy protection from ISP tracking and data selling.
Regularly check your ISP's privacy policy for changes - many ISPs update their data collection practices without prominent notification.
Use multiple DNS providers across different devices to avoid creating a single point of failure in your privacy setup.
Monitor your internet speeds after changing DNS settings - if speeds drop significantly, try a different DNS provider closer to your location.
Consider using Incognito Browser alongside encrypted DNS for comprehensive protection against both ISP tracking and website tracking scripts.

faqs.question: Can my ISP still track me if I use encrypted DNS?
faqs.answer: Encrypted DNS prevents your ISP from seeing which specific pages you visit, but they can still see the main domains you connect to through IP addresses. For complete protection, combine encrypted DNS with a VPN.

faqs.question: Will changing my DNS settings slow down my internet?
faqs.answer: Good encrypted DNS providers like Cloudflare often provide faster DNS resolution than your ISP's servers. You may actually see improved browsing speeds, especially for the first visit to websites.

faqs.question: Is it legal for ISPs to sell my browsing data?
faqs.answer: In the US, ISPs can legally sell your browsing data unless you explicitly opt out. The rules vary by country, but most ISPs worldwide collect and monetize browsing data in some form.

faqs.question: How do I know if my ISP is throttling my connection?
faqs.answer: Run speed tests before and after changing DNS settings, and compare speeds when accessing different types of content. Significant variations may indicate throttling based on your browsing activity.

faqs.question: Can I use different DNS providers for different devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can mix DNS providers across devices. This can actually improve privacy by not centralizing all your DNS queries with one provider, though it makes troubleshooting more complex.

faqs.question: What's the difference between DNS over HTTPS and regular encrypted DNS?
faqs.answer: DNS over HTTPS (DoH) encrypts DNS queries within regular web traffic, making it harder for ISPs to block or detect. Regular encrypted DNS uses dedicated protocols that ISPs can more easily identify and potentially block.
